name: Cuewright
positioning: Cuewright is the prompt workshop for knowledge workers who want reusable, labelled prompt patterns instead of one-off guesses typed into a chat box.
audience: Writers, product people, analysts and small teams who use AI assistants daily and are tired of rewriting the same vague request three times.
strategy: Position prompting as a craft with tools, templates and a bench, not a magic trick. Lead with annotated before/after examples and a free weekly clinic to build trust, then convert to the paid Cue Library and team shelves.

contrastPairs.use: large display type and graphics only

designSystem.spacing: 8px base grid; sections breathe at 96-128px desktop, 64px mobile; notebook ruled-line rhythm of 28px
designSystem.radius: 12-28px on cards and keycaps, 999px only on small tag pills
designSystem.borders: Solid 2-3px graphite outlines on cards and buttons; dashed hairlines for blueprint guides and dividers
designSystem.imagery: No photography. Inline SVG prompt cards, keycaps, blueprint grids and hand-drawn-style annotation arrows
designSystem.shapes: Rounded rectangles offset over a solid orange or graphite 'shadow card'; circular stamp marks
designSystem.buttons: Graphite or orange slabs with a hard offset shadow and a blinking caret block; press state drops the offset
designSystem.cards: Prompt cards with a title bar, labelled mono lines (ROLE / TASK / LIMITS) and a caret on the last line
designSystem.motifs: Cursor carets, blueprint dimension arrows, keyboard keycaps, WORKSHOP TESTED stamps, notebook margin rule

artDirection: Every creative should feel like a page torn from a careful maker's notebook: paper ground, a ruled or blueprint grid, one hero prompt card and a few annotations explaining it. Instrument Serif carries the voice with an orange italic turn of phrase; Geist Mono carries anything a user would actually type. Use orange sparingly for carets, arrows and stamps, never for small text on light grounds. Alternate light paper, peach and charcoal grounds so the feed reads as one bench with different lighting.
